data.text:
I searched each claim.

**Claim 0: one inch of rain on a 1,000 square foot roof sheds about 623 gallons. Supported as written (the theoretical total).**
- Hakaru rain barrel guide: the constant is 0.623 gallons per square foot per inch (1/12 x 7.48). URL: https://www.hakaru.io/guides/rain-barrel-calculator-guide
- Las Virgenes Municipal Water District: 0.62 x 1,000 = 620 gallons every time it rains an inch. URL: https://lvmwd.com/home/showpublisheddocument/12631/637275594930470000
- HowStuffWorks: about 625 gallons per inch on 1,000 square feet. URL: https://home.howstuffworks.com/rain-barrel2.htm
- Real collection is lower (about 520 to 600 gallons) after losses. 'Over 600 gallons' fits the raw figure.

**Claim 1: asphalt shingles are the most common roofing material on US homes. Supported as written.**
- Home Innovation Research Labs roofing market trends: asphalt shingles dominate re-roofing and new homes. URL: https://www.homeinnovation.com/insights/trends_data/roofing-market-trends-weve-got-you-covered-and-re-covered/43371
- GAF: asphalt shingles cover more than 80 percent of US homes (industry figure). URL: https://www.gaf.com/en-us/blog/your-home/what-are-shingles-made-of-1ff099ad-ad65-43f6-8b5a-d5f9e41cd3ff
- Estimates range 70 to 85 percent.

**Claim 2: shingles are laid in overlapping rows from the bottom edge so each row covers the joints of the row below. Supported in a corrected form.**
- IKO starter course bulletin: the starter course at the eave fills the spaces under the first course's cutouts and joints; joints must not align. URL: https://www.iko.com/na/document/tbr57-shingle-installation-starter-course-product-bulletin
- Fine Homebuilding, The Starter Course: joints are staggered so they are covered by the course above. URL: https://www.finehomebuilding.com/project-guides/roofing/the-starter-course
- Corrected: "Shingles are laid from the bottom edge up, each row overlapping the one below with the joints staggered."
